mechanisms.title: Unassigned No-Fit Hearts Above Maximum Annulus Coverage (> 27 mm)
mechanisms.explanation: Of the 93 hearts with no fit due to the annulus-coverage rule, 67 hearts have an annulus diameter exceeding the 27 mm maximum limit of the largest valve size (27 mm nominal). These 67 hearts fall into the 26-28 mm (30 no-fit hearts), 28-30 mm (31 no-fit hearts), and 30-32 mm (6 no-fit hearts) annulus bands. Profiling these 67 hearts shows a group mean annulusMm of 28.3736793853115 mm compared to 23.8792463929575 mm for the rest of the cohort (effect size 1.81723566064299), along with globally larger aortic root dimensions including lvotMm (group mean 29.1834336521146 mm vs 23.203976777729 mm, effect size 1.7786767322157), sinusMm (group mean 36.9204307212132 mm vs 32.0044153506555 mm, effect size 1.47632360958678), sinotubularJunctionMm (group mean 32.6361463160546 mm vs 28.9495116935805 mm, effect size 1.27311068487743), lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio (group mean 1.05926460340551 vs 0.943450315423325, effect size 1.08050778051756), aorticValveArea (group mean 81.5480622670355 vs 60.6312620342401, effect size 0.960191953912409), sinusHeightMm (group mean 27.5373134328358 mm vs 24.6966966966967 mm, effect size 0.852170347659889), and angleDeg (group mean 30.3549915069439 deg vs 26.3529684044269 deg, effect size 0.419329496520048). For example, heart-019 has an annulusMm of 27.3588421207855 mm, failing the 27 mm limit by a margin of -0.358842120785503 mm.

These 26 hearts fall into the 18-20 mm (6 no-fit hearts) and 20-22 mm (20 no-fit hearts) annulus bands. mechanisms.title: Sinotubular Junction (STJ) Excess Risk from Narrow STJ Relative to Assigned Valve Size
mechanisms.explanation: 52 hearts are placed at risk by the stj-excess rule across all three valve sizes (23, 25, and 27 mm). Inspection of individual hearts reveals that each nominal valve size requires the sinotubularJunctionMm (STJ) to be at least nominalMm + 2 mm (limit 25 mm for size 23 in heart-018, 27 mm for size 25 in heart-086, and 29 mm for size 27 in heart-014). Profiling the 52 failing hearts shows that while their annulusMm is similar to the rest of the cohort (group mean 24.2162817933461 mm vs 24.6941922828066 mm, effect size -0.193233715024884), they have a substantially narrower sinotubularJunctionMm (group mean 26.5045097370466 mm vs 30.0246399161251 mm, difference -3.52013017907853 mm, effect size -1.2156114728117), a narrower sinusMm (group mean 30.5892482692222 mm vs 33.1623513220977 mm, difference -2.57310305287558 mm, effect size -0.772725978362664), and a higher lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio (group mean 1.02645440665182 vs 0.953344983673109, effect size 0.682085964814614). Thus, hearts with disproportionate outflow/annulus sizing relative to a constricted STJ receive a valve size whose outflow frame exceeds the available STJ diameter.

38 hearts are placed at risk by the sinus-clearance rule across all three valve sizes. Inspection of individual hearts shows that each nominal valve size requires sinusMm to be at least nominalMm + 5 mm (limit 28 mm for size 23 in heart-018, 30 mm for size 25 in heart-086, and 32 mm for size 27 in heart-014). Profiling these 38 hearts demonstrates markedly smaller sinus dimensions despite qualifying for the 21-27 mm annulus range: sinusMm is much narrower (group mean 29.0481355368023 mm vs 33.2246133140638 mm, difference -4.17647777726146 mm, effect size -1.25423382205296), sinotubularJunctionMm is narrower (group mean 26.7830986506325 mm vs 29.8592581447899 mm, difference -3.07615949415738 mm, effect size -1.06229445590425), and sinusHeightMm is shorter (group mean 22.0921052631579 mm vs 25.4958563535912 mm, difference -3.40375109043327 mm, effect size -1.02110774508236), while lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio is elevated (group mean 1.02620177062988 vs 0.956198939724312, effect size 0.653102521023595). When a valve is selected based solely on annulusMm in hearts with shallow, narrow sinuses, the assigned nominal size leaves insufficient sinus clearance.
